opening.text: A plane reaches a busy airport and the pilot hears the radio: “Hold your position.” So the plane circles. Passengers look at their watches. Nobody likes it. But the pilot is not forgotten. The controller sees the whole sky and knows when the runway will be clear.
Most of us have spent time in a holding pattern. We have prayed for something and the answer has not come yet. Let us look at what God and His servants teach about waiting.

mainMessage.text: Waiting is not the same as being ignored. God sees more than we can see. He knows the right time, and He stays close while we wait.

blocks.text: **The tower sees more than we do.** From the cockpit, the runway looks empty. The controller can see what the pilot cannot. God sees the whole picture of our lives. Sometimes the wait is because He is preparing the way, or preparing us.

And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
In my life I have learned that sometimes I do not receive an answer to a prayer because the Lord knows I am not ready.
The delay may be care, not silence.

**The pattern can be long.** Some holds last a few minutes. Some last much longer. The same is true of the waits in our lives. The scripture says the answer will come at the appointed time, even if it seems slow.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The path to holiness and happiness here and hereafter is a long and sometimes rocky one.
A long road is still a road that leads somewhere.

**The voice on the radio is kind.** The controller is not working against the pilot. The controller is working for a safe landing. In the same way, the One who asks us to wait is full of mercy. He is on our side.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
He is pure love, gloriously personified, and Merciful Father is His name.
We wait with a Father who loves us.
**No plane in the pattern is forgotten.** Every aircraft in the holding pattern is on the controller’s screen. God knows each of us by name. He knows what the waiting costs us.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
He knows your sacrifices and your sorrows.
Nothing about our waiting is hidden from Him.

**Stay in the air.** A pilot who gives up and turns off the engines in a holding pattern will not land safely. Our part is to keep going. We keep praying, keep serving and keep trusting. The Lord will be faithful to us.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us not give up on the Lord.
We keep flying.

**Peace while circling.** A good pilot is calm in the pattern because the pilot trusts the tower. We can have that calm too. Peace does not wait until the answer comes. It can come while we are still waiting.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
His peace and rest will be yours as you continue to wait upon Him in faith.
He offers rest now.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they had to wait on the Lord. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Simeon Waits for the Savior

blocks.text: Simeon was told he would see the Christ before he died. He waited, and kept being faithful. Then one day the promise was kept.

And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
Simeon did not give up. He kept waiting, and the promise came to pass.

application.text: First, name one thing you are waiting for. Tell God plainly how the waiting feels.
Second, choose one thing to keep doing while you wait. It may be a prayer, a small act of service or a daily scripture.
Third, trust that God has not forgotten you. If the wait feels heavy, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God hears our prayers, even when the answer is slow. I know that He sees what we cannot see. I have felt His peace while I was still waiting. I know that Jesus Christ is near to those who wait on Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

versions.analogy: A plane in a holding pattern

opening.text: Imagine a train platform on a cold morning. The board says the train is late. You check your watch. You pace. You wonder if you should give up and walk. But the train is on its way. It runs on a schedule you cannot see, and it will arrive.
Waiting on the Lord can feel like that platform. Let us see what we can learn about waiting well.

mainMessage.text: The Lord keeps a schedule for each of us, and His timing is good. While we wait, He is near. We do not need to leave the platform. We can stay, trust and rest.

blocks.text: **The train runs on a schedule we cannot see.** The people on the platform only see an empty track. The train crew sees the whole line. God sees the whole line of our lives. Sometimes we wait because the track ahead is not yet ready, or because we are not.

And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
In my life I have learned that sometimes I do not receive an answer to a prayer because the Lord knows I am not ready.
The delay may hold a purpose.
**Some waits are long.** Some trains are a few minutes late. Some are hours late. Our waits can be long too. The scripture tells us the promise will come at the appointed time, even when it tarries.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The path to holiness and happiness here and hereafter is a long and sometimes rocky one.
The track is long, and it leads somewhere good.
**The One who runs the line is kind.** A good conductor cares about the people on the platform. Our Father in Heaven cares about each one of us. His delays are not careless. He is gentle with us.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
He is pure love, gloriously personified, and Merciful Father is His name.
The One we wait for is merciful.
**He knows who is on the platform.** The station staff knows every ticket holder. The Savior knows each one of us too. He knows what we gave up to be here. He knows our tears.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
He knows your sacrifices and your sorrows.
We are seen on the platform.

**Do not walk off the platform.** The worst thing to do when a train is late is to leave and miss it. Giving up too soon can cost us what we were waiting for. Faithful waiting means we stay where the Lord can find us.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us not give up on the Lord.
We stay where He can find us.

**Sit down and rest.** You do not have to stand on the platform with a tight jaw. You can sit down, breathe and rest. Peace does not depend on the train arriving. The Savior offers rest to us now, while we wait.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
His peace and rest will be yours as you continue to wait upon Him in faith.
Rest can come before the answer does.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they waited and the promise came. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Abraham and Sarah Receive the Promise

blocks.text: Abraham and Sarah had waited many years for the son God promised. It seemed too late. But God had set a time, and He kept His word.
And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did unto Sarah as he had spoken. For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
The promise came at the set time. It came in God’s time, not theirs.

application.text: First, write down what you are waiting for. Then write one reason you believe God can still keep His promises to you.
Second, pick a way to rest while you wait. It could be a walk, a quiet prayer or a favorite hymn.
Third, stay where you are faithful. Keep the commandments and keep showing up. If waiting is wearing you down, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Lord’s timing is good, even when I cannot see why. I know He knows my name and my sorrows. I have found rest in Him while I waited. I know that He keeps His promises. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A good stew cannot be rushed. You put the pot on low heat, cover it and leave it. Turn the heat up and the meat turns tough. Open the lid every few minutes and the heat escapes. The best thing you can do is wait. When the time is right, the food is tender and full of flavor.
Some things in life need that kind of slow, patient heat. Let us see what the Lord teaches us about waiting for them.

mainMessage.text: Some blessings are ready only after time has passed. The Lord does not delay to be unkind. He knows when the work is done. We can trust Him with the time.

blocks.text: **Some things are not ready yet.** A cook knows when the stew is not done. We cannot always see that for ourselves. God sees what is not yet ready, and sometimes that includes us.

And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
In my life I have learned that sometimes I do not receive an answer to a prayer because the Lord knows I am not ready.
The wait can be part of the preparing.
**Slow cooking takes hours.** No one hurries a stew. The scripture says that the promise comes at the appointed time, even if it feels slow. Long waits are part of the way some blessings come.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The path to holiness and happiness here and hereafter is a long and sometimes rocky one.
A long cook is not a wasted cook.

**The cook cares about the meal.** A cook does not slow the pot out of spite. A cook slows it because the meal matters. Our Father in Heaven is like that. He is a loving parent, and He cares about the outcome.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
He is pure love, gloriously personified, and Merciful Father is His name.
We can wait with trust in His love.
**The cook knows what it costs.** A good cook knows how hungry the family is. The Lord knows the cost of our waiting too. He knows the long nights and the quiet prayers.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
He knows your sacrifices and your sorrows.
He has not missed any of it.

**Keep the lid on.** If you keep lifting the lid, the heat leaks out and the meal takes longer. Giving up on God partway through the wait works against us. Faith means we stay with the process and trust Him.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us not give up on the Lord.
We stay with Him.
**Enjoy the quiet kitchen.** While the stew simmers, the house fills with a good smell. The wait can be peaceful too. The Lord offers us rest as we wait, if we turn to Him.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
His peace and rest will be yours as you continue to wait upon Him in faith.
The waiting can be a quiet place.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when waiting turned into a blessing. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Hannah Receives Her Son

blocks.text: Hannah prayed for a child for years. She poured out her heart at the temple. Eli the priest blessed her, and in time her prayer was answered.

Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord.
Hannah kept asking, and she kept trusting. The answer came when the time was right.

application.text: First, tell God what you are hoping for. Then tell Him you are willing to wait for His timing.
Second, use the waiting for something good. Serve someone, study or build a habit that will help you later.
Third, watch for small signs that He is working. If the waiting feels like too much, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God hears us and that His timing is wise. I know that good things take time. I have learned that waiting on Him is never wasted. I know that Jesus Christ is with us in every season. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: You drop a letter in the mailbox. Then you wait. A day goes by, then a week. You wonder if it got lost. But the letter is moving. It goes from truck to sorting room to truck again. You cannot see it, but it is on its way.
Our prayers can feel like that letter. We send them up and then we wait. Let us look at what we can trust while we do.

mainMessage.text: A prayer is never lost. God receives every one. His answer may come in a way or at a time we do not expect. Our task is to keep trusting while it travels.

blocks.text: **The letter may not be ready to arrive.** A letter can only be delivered when someone is there to open the door. God may wait to answer until we are ready to receive it. His timing is a kind of care.

And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
In my life I have learned that sometimes I do not receive an answer to a prayer because the Lord knows I am not ready.
The delay can be a form of kindness.
**Some mail takes the long way.** A letter sent far away can take weeks. The scripture promises that what God has said will come at the appointed time, even if it feels slow.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The path to holiness and happiness here and hereafter is a long and sometimes rocky one.
A long route can still arrive.
**The One who receives it is kind.** Think of the person at the other end. They are glad to hear from you. Heavenly Father is glad to hear from us. He answers out of love.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
He is pure love, gloriously personified, and Merciful Father is His name.
Every prayer lands with a Father who loves us.
**Every letter has our name on it.** Mail is addressed to a person. Our prayers are known to God by name. He knows what is written inside, and what it cost us to write it.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
He knows your sacrifices and your sorrows.
Nothing we send is overlooked.

**Do not recall the letter.** Once a letter is on its way, taking it back only causes more delay. In the same way, giving up on prayer closes the door on what could come. We keep the faith and let the answer arrive.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us not give up on the Lord.
We keep trusting.

**Rest while it travels.** You cannot make a letter go faster by staring at the mailbox. You can go about your day. The Savior invites us to rest in Him while we wait. We can do our daily work and know that the answer is coming.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
His peace and rest will be yours as you continue to wait upon Him in faith.
We can live our day with peace.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were still waiting and God stayed close. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph Is Remembered at Last

blocks.text: Joseph helped the chief butler in prison. But the butler forgot him. Joseph waited in a dungeon for a long time. Then, at the right moment, he was called out.

Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him. Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.
Joseph felt forgotten, but God had not forgotten him. The release came when God’s plan was ready.

application.text: First, bring your waiting to God in a short prayer today. Say it as you would write to someone you trust.
Second, keep your daily work going. Do the next right thing in front of you.
Third, when you feel forgotten, remember Joseph. If the wait is heavy, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that no prayer is lost. I know that God hears each one and answers in His time. I have felt Him near when I felt forgotten. I know that Jesus Christ is faithful to those who wait. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Anyone who has kept watch through the night knows how long the hours before dawn can feel. It is dark and quiet, and the clock barely moves. But the sun is already on its way. It has never once failed to rise. The night is real, and so is the morning.
Waiting on the Lord can feel like those dark hours. Let us see what we can hold on to until the light comes.

mainMessage.text: The dawn is certain. God keeps His promises, and He keeps them at the right time. While we wait through the night, we are not alone.

blocks.text: **The sun is already on its way.** The night does not mean the sun has gone. It means we cannot see it yet. God’s answer may already be moving toward us. Sometimes we need the night to become ready for the light.

And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
In my life I have learned that sometimes I do not receive an answer to a prayer because the Lord knows I am not ready.
The night has a purpose.
**Some nights are long.** A winter night can feel endless. So can a season of waiting. The scripture says the vision will come at the appointed time, even if it seems to tarry.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The path to holiness and happiness here and hereafter is a long and sometimes rocky one.
The long night still ends.
**Dawn comes from a loving hand.** The morning is not luck. It is a gift. The One who sends the dawn is the same One who loves us. His mercy is behind every sunrise.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting on the Lord” from the October 2020 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
He is pure love, gloriously personified, and Merciful Father is His name.
The light comes from love.
**Someone is keeping watch with us.** A watch is easier when you are not alone. The Savior knows the dark hours. He knows what our waiting has cost, and He stays near.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
He knows your sacrifices and your sorrows.
We are not on watch alone.
**Do not leave the watch.** The hour before sunrise is when many people give up. Staying at the post is a quiet kind of faith. The Lord renews those who wait for Him.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us not give up on the Lord.
We hold our post.
**Rest in the quiet.** The night is not only dark. It can be still and peaceful too. We do not need to strain against it. The Savior gives us rest while we wait for the light.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Waiting upon the Lord: Thy Will Be Done” from the October 2011 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
His peace and rest will be yours as you continue to wait upon Him in faith.
The quiet can hold peace.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when the light finally came after a long wait. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Zacharias Is Told His Prayer Is Heard

blocks.text: Zacharias and Elisabeth had prayed for a child for a very long time. They were old. Then an angel appeared with news.
But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
Their prayer had been heard all along. The answer came when God’s time had come.

application.text: First, name your “long night.” Tell God that you are staying on watch.
Second, do one thing each day that shows you trust Him. It can be small.
Third, look back and notice where He has already helped you. Let that carry you forward. If you need support, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the morning comes. I know that God keeps His promises, even when the night is long. I have felt Him near in the dark hours. I know that Jesus Christ is the light that comes after the wait. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
